title: A named skill is the one that was reviewed
description: Follows SG1 on the same integration branch. The study report (quality-gates-internal reports/2026-11-16-agent-skills) holds the evidence: the headless route records a digest of each skill file after the session and nothing compares it; the subagent route does not resolve a named skill before the spawn. The main branch has since changed how a missing review skill is handled on the review route, so each task of this phase reads the main branch's current behaviour before it is written in full.
desiredOutcome: A plan can pin the content of a skill it names, and a pinned skill whose content changed stops a session before it starts, with the skill named; a skill a plan names that does not resolve stops the subagent route the way it stops the headless route; a guide says how to vendor an outside skill; and the low findings of the SG1 review are fixed or recorded as not reproducing.

findings.issue: The not-run half of cf31c/cf31d is recorded through _harness.skip(check, other, ..., True): `absent` is the constant True, so the helper failing direction (skipped on a host that has the mechanism) can never fire. The half is chosen by the same top_folds read that picks the half that ran, so it is true by construction, but on a mixed volume (project tree folds and .claude tells case apart, or the reverse) cf31c label still says `on a real volume that folds case` while only the folder row is held, and nothing marks the mixed case as neither kind. Only SKIPPED HERE is printed, so a reader cannot tell a mixed volume from a plain one except through the printed pair of folds answers.
findings.resolution: Pass the evidence the helper asks for (for the not-run half, the negation of the disk read that selected the other half), and when top_folds != cdir_folds label the case as the mixed volume rather than as either kind.

findings.issue: The cf29 budget for a write that creates its file allows `links` = len(rel) extra calls (2) while the measured extra by the question own source is 1 (cf-new.ts: 4 before, 5 now, allowance 2, in after.folding.out). A single disk call added to that write path still passes `within` (6 <= 6); only the call-for-call comparisons `now == today` and `now == off` catch it, so the claim that the budget is what turns an added call red holds for the existing-file write (allowance 0, exact) but not for the creating one. The mutation row for a disk call added to the config question path went red through the call-for-call half, not the budget.
findings.resolution: Say in the comment above _before (the call-for-call paragraph) that the added calls of a creating write are held by `now == today`, not by the budget; or tighten the allowance to the measured link count per host once windows CI has printed it.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: acceptance (1) and rule 1 say that on every host a builder that kept GIT_DIR leaves the other repository unchanged. kept_gitdir_faults() (line 1140) waives the unchanged check whenever refused_by_check(built) is true, so on a host where git lets the patched builder commit into the other repository (macOS) and the check then refuses with exit 3, esc47 asserts only not-exit-0 and a documented failure. The unconditional unchanged reading remains only for the shipped builder (esc45, esc46). The diff is honest about this: the block comment (1038-1048), the esc47 label (unless its own-repository check refused the build) and the executor outcome all say so, and the old esc47 never asserted anything about the other repository, so nothing is asserted more weakly than before. But the task text as written is not what the case holds, and a patched builder that writes the other repository and then refuses passes esc47 by design. I did not rerun the executor probe_victim.py to see the macOS write myself; the order is consistent with build-shop.sh (built() runs after every commit) and with the executor mutation rows.
findings.resolution: No code change needed if the owner accepts the narrowing: amend acceptance (1), or record it as a reconciled divergence, to say unchanged unconditionally for the shipped builder (esc45/esc46); for a GIT_DIR-keeping patch, unchanged unless the own-repository check refused. If the clause must stand literally, the only way is a patched builder that stops before git writes, which is not esc47 subject.

findings.issue: check_reached() reads as not reached any exit 2 whose stderr has build-shop: git init|add|commit failed, whatever git own words were, and the skip goes through _harness.skip(..., True): the absent argument is the constant True, so the helper failure direction (skipped where the mechanism exists) can never fire. On a host where a patched builder fails at a git step for an unrelated reason, esc57 prints SKIPPED HERE and passes; only esc47 weaker conditions and esc58 (check held without GIT_DIR) remain. The words are printed in the label, so it is findable, but nothing requires them to be the work-tree refusal.
findings.resolution: Optional: have the esc57 skip branch also require git own words to name a work tree or GIT_DIR (a constant next to WINDOWS_WORDS), so an unrelated git failure fails esc57 instead of skipping it; or pass a computed absent argument that is not constant True.

findings.issue: The wiring from the whole-span judgement to a fault - `if grew > bound: faults.append(...)` in timing_faults - is held by no case that can go red without it. esc66, esc67 and esc68 call span_growth directly (lines 2006, 2033, 2055) and never timing_faults; its only caller is the real-engine pass at 2141, which is green for linear texts with or without that branch. The backtracking mutation rows go red by `killed at the 10s deadline`, not by `grew ... bound`, and no row mutates that branch. By reading, deleting the `if grew > bound` block leaves 76/76 green: the growth judgement is exercised as a pure function but not as the gate (the wiring of the ceiling is held - the 1 ms row reddens esc53 and esc55 - the wiring of the growth fault is not). It is the only real-engine path for a polynomial cost between the power of the bound and the ceiling: an exponent from 1.5 to about 1.9 whose time at 51200 units stays under 1.0 s (kinds 1, 7, 8 read about 0.26 s at n**1.7 on windows numbers), which neither the ceiling nor the deadline catches.
findings.resolution: Add a case that feeds timing_faults hand-built `runs` (name, counted, lengths, a mapping from engine to result): one with the lengths and times of the windows history (expect no fault, least room 2.87) and one with the same lengths and a quadratic series (expect a `grew ... bound` fault and least under 1); add a mutation row that removes the `if grew > bound:` block and expects that case red.

findings.issue: TRIPWIRE_POWER is held only inside a window by the new cases: esc66 needs the windows history to pass (power at least about 1.3) and a per-doubling read above 2 ** power (4.16 > 2 ** power, so power under about 2.06); the quadratic of esc68 is caught while the length ratio to the power stays under 59 thousand (power under about 1.97). A power of 1.9 survives every case by reading, though the task keeps the power unmoved. The mutation row raises it to 2.5 only.
findings.resolution: Give esc68 a second cost, a power law at 1.75 anchored the same way, so a power raised past it goes red.

findings.issue: The load headroom of the ceiling and the room are argued from figures the evidence does not fully carry. (a) `about 0.63 s under such load` scales the 800-unit busy/idle ratio 2.35 from the 2026-11-19 CI log (not handed to me, not read) onto the 51200-unit search, while S/diag4/diag_windows_2025.txt:159,215,255 measure that search idle and loaded directly: 0.1875 s, 0.2031 s and 0.2656 s (1.42x). (b) The comment gives 2.87 as the least room; the suite run of its own on the windows runner read 2.83 (S/diag4/diag_windows_2025.txt:378, esc53), so readings span 2.83 to 3.66 and the margin to the factor of two is narrower than the comment reads. (c) `the longest text there is ... 1883359 characters` is a present-tense count with no command beside it; the stale check of esc66 guards the 1883333 of the history row, not the 26 characters of the twin added to it.
findings.resolution: Write the measured loaded figure beside or instead of the extrapolated 2.35, add the 2.83 reading to the room sentence as history, and carry the expression that prints the length of the longest text, or drop the figure.

findings.issue: One TRIPWIRE_CEILING serves both engines. Node longest search reads 0.005 to 0.009 s on the windows runner (diag4:158,214,254), so 1.0 s is 100 to 200 times its idle figure and catches for node nothing the deadline and the growth judgement (room about 15) do not; for python it catches only a search of about 1 to 2 s (past that, four searches exceed the 8 s series deadline first), a guard 5x over the idle 0.19-0.27 s.
findings.resolution: Derive a ceiling per engine (for node from its own loaded 0.0093 s), or say in the comment that the ceiling is python and node is held by growth and the deadline.

findings.issue: esc70 hand-built runs give repeats None in _answered, the shape of the node child. The python child always sends a list (diag_windows_2025.txt: repeats [2134, 2]), so the growth fault the real python pass produces carries the suffix ", over [..] searches a length" (timing_faults 1957-1960). esc70 builds its owed text without that suffix, so deleting the suffix, or breaking its formatting, leaves every case green: a branch of the growth fault the real pass uses is held by no case.
findings.resolution: Let _answered take a repeats argument and give the cost at the 1.75 power a list as the python child sends it (for example [3, 2]); build the owed text with the suffix ", over [3, 2] searches a length", so the whole growth fault the real python pass emits is compared.

findings.issue: The twenty block figures of the two suites (and the two file figures, which are their sums) are this machine's macOS seconds under `platform: windows-2025`. I confirmed they equal sg2.8/sweep-costs.after-local.json (platform darwin) entry for entry, and that the committed table is identical to sg2.8/after/sweep-costs.json, so nothing is hand-edited beyond the two recorded commands; the other block figures cannot be checked here and come from the windows logs by the executor's account. What the mixed table does: (a) block_timeout is max(300, ceil(3 x figure)). Every one of the twenty comes out at the 300 s floor, ge-generated 71.4 -> 215 -> 300, jw-generated 60.6 -> 182 -> 300. A windows-recorded figure for ge-generated (about 235 s or more) would give about 705 s, the same rule that gives ar18-block 706 s. So the one block that matters keeps the 300 s that killed the whole suite twice, with the other nine blocks' seconds removed from it and nothing else. (b) shard_units deals by slot-seconds, and these twenty are weighed on a scale roughly three times lighter than every neighbour: ge-generated at 71.4 sorts below drive_phase's ab-block (123.1), though its windows seconds are about the size of ar18-block's 235.1, so it is not dealt among the heaviest first and the part that gets it is under-counted by roughly 160 s per suite. (c) The runner's own comment above load_costs says a timeout reads the figure itself and a darwin figure under-states a windows one, which is exactly this. No case could have gone red: the table has one `platform` field and no per-entry origin, and swp4 only checks that the field names a windows family. The executor's choice of `--costs-from-log ... --platform windows-2025` over a bare local `--record-costs` was right (the local write set platform darwin, which swp4 refuses), but merge_costs then kept the local block figures under the new label. The task text's own premise ('the table's figures are this machine's') was wrong about the table.
findings.resolution: Before this closes as green on the windows leg, record the twenty blocks from the first windows logs that carry them (`--costs-from-log ... --platform windows-2025 --record-costs`), and until then say in the closing note that the twenty figures are macOS. If the coordinator wants the table to state only what it knows, leave the two suites' blocks out of `blocks` so block_figure answers 'untimed' and block_timeout gives each the largest timeout any entry gives (706 s) - an honest basis and more headroom than the floor, at the price of the deal using the median estimate. Do not hand-scale the figures.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 6 ('If a single block is itself heavier than the others together ... say so and split it where the seam is; do not raise a timeout to make a slow file fit'). The executor says so and does not split. I checked the arithmetic: ge-generated 71.4 vs the other nine 23.5 (94.9 - 71.4), jw-generated 60.6 vs 34.2 (94.8 - 60.6): both right, both heavier than the rest together. Against the logs: guard 236.1 s windows plain 1 (ci2 run-44573316400.log line 7938) against 31.6 s linux plain 1 (line 6238); in ci4 job-136040228539.log line 365 the same suite is killed at 300.0 s and job-136040228761.log line 367 kills journal at 300.0 s. A kill is a lower bound, not a measurement. The executor's 'at 3.3x ... about 236 s and 200 s, 0.79 and 0.67 of the timeout' treats the lower bound of the ratio (300/92) as its value; a suite killed at 300 s has a generated block of at least about 0.78 x 300 = 234 s, and the same leg went from 236 s to 300 s or more between runs, so the margin under the 300 s block timeout is not demonstrated. The local 92 s itself was taken with two suites sharing a loaded machine (the executor's own load figures 2.6-6.8, fseventsd at 90-180 percent), against 31.6 and 42.1 s on linux CI. Whether the staging was worth doing: it is not pointless - it takes the other 22-33 percent of each suite out of the block that can be killed, runs the nine small blocks in parallel (wall 91.5 s to 73.8 s locally), and it is what lets the table calibrate the block once windows figures exist - but with finding 1 standing it buys only that 22-33 percent against an unchanged 300 s, so the next windows run can fail the same way. The fixture-cost option the executor lists as (b) (a template repository copied per world; his profile: 27.7 s of 73.3 s building 364 worlds with 1497 repository-tool calls, about 20 s in the hook's own calls) keeps every label and was not tried; the seam in gen_sweep (tests/test_guard_edits.py:2462, each world built and visited independently) exists but cf36's single label summarises the whole sweep, so a split that keeps labels needs an aggregation the harness does not offer.
findings.resolution: Close this task with the open item as a plan task of its own, not as prose in a return: cut the generated-arrangements sweep's fixture cost (template-copy worlds, or per-family cases with new ids and an agreed label change), acceptance a measured windows figure for ge-generated and jw-generated well under the block timeout, or a timeout calibrated from a windows figure (finding 1). Record the open item against the phase so sign-off sees it; do not raise the timeout.

findings.issue: Answer to question 2: (a) for what cf37b's label says, with a residue. I ran the executor's probe_listing.py in a scratch directory: a cold process's first ordinary decide lists scripts/, scripts/config, scripts/git and scripts/governance (os.scandir, found by _config.find_script's os.walk while _load_journal_lib loads _journal_io.py), the second call lists none, and after `_config.journal_lib()` the first lists none. guard-edits.py reaches that load on an ordinary write through `_config.in_journal` (guard-edits.py:461, tree inside the project), so the comment's claim is true: those listings are a lookup of the plugin's own code, not the config question (the registrations the cf29-cf37 family counts). Separating them is correct, and the assertion's condition is unchanged. But before the change cf37b had only ever measured a warm process by accident, and it now does so on purpose; the shipped hook is a fresh process per call and pays the four-folder walk on every ordinary write. No case anywhere asserts that cold figure, so a growth in it (a fifth folder, a second walk) would be green. The cost existed before this diff and the diff does not add it, which is why this is not med, but this diff is what makes the suite blind to it. The executor reported it in his outcome as a batch finding; nothing in the tree records it.
findings.resolution: Route it to sign-off as a finding: add one case that counts the listings of a cold hook process for an ordinary write (the hook as a subprocess, as cf37 already does for its processes) and pins the measured number with its basis, or give find_script a direct path for the journal library so the walk is not paid per call.

findings.issue: Two sentences claim more than the code shows. 'sn0 is the name that report carried before the suite was staged': before the change the raising block was reported as `sn0 the switch-reading cases` (the removed stage call labelled that way), now it is reported as `sn0`, so the name is shortened, not carried. 'nearly all of it is `oq5`' is a ratio with no basis in the file; its basis (a profile, oq5 50.5 s of 53.3 s) is only in the filed return.
findings.resolution: Say 'a label beginning sn0, as before' or drop the sentence, and either carry the basis (the command that profiled the block) or delete 'nearly all of it' and keep the pointer to oq5.

findings.issue: cf36e puts its measured values (commit ids, object-file counts, lists) into the case LABEL, not the check's third detail argument. Its PASS line is about 1.2 kB and differs on every run (the commit ids move with the commit's second), where every other label of the suite is stable text. Anything that compares labels across runs (the before/after label comparison this task's rule 3 uses, a replay, a credit by label) sees a different case each time.
findings.resolution: Keep the label to the static sentence and pass the as_template ... placed values as the detail argument: check(label, cond, detail).

findings.issue: The third template - the initialised-only repository _gen_init copies into nested-repo, repo and link-repo worlds - is held by no case: cf36e copies only the top template for independence and checks member placement for top and down; nothing asserts that a copy of the init template names no commit. The mutation table has rows for link, hard link, uncommitted template and wrong member template, none for the init template given a committed repository. The records comparison would not tell either, because the hook does not read those repositories' heads.
findings.resolution: Add to cf36e (or beside it) a copy of the init template read with _gen_repo_state asserting head None and an empty object count, and a mutation row giving _gen_init the committed template; show it red.

findings.issue: The section comment says a repository 'records nothing of where it stands' and that its index is 'the same bytes wherever git made them'. The index records each file's stat data (inode, ctime, mtime, device), so a copied index is stale against the copy's files; it stays correct only because the first status re-hashes. cf36e does show status clean for the copy, so the behaviour is held, but the sentence claims more than is true.
findings.resolution: Say that the index's stat data is stale in a copy and that a status re-hashes (cf36e reads it clean), instead of saying nothing records the place.

The re-record the task says is owed from a log of the changed code exists only in the executor's return prose: I found no task or note in docs/audit/phases/SG2.json that carries it.

tasks.title: The low findings of the SG1 review, in one batch
tasks.description:
The review of phase SG1 (five slices, each finding re-run by the orchestrator where it says so) and the reviewers of its tasks left low findings. None held the sign-off. They are fixed here together, each with a case that is red before its fix, or recorded as not reproducing with the run that shows it. A finding marked unconfirmed below was read, not run: run it first.

FROM THE TASK REVIEWERS (recorded on the phase as SG1-R2 to SG1-R7).
R2. A floor block typed by an agent is dropped by submit only; a return filed through the file-return verb with a typed, marked block is read back as the script's reading. The README row on the floor guard and reference/execute-task.md say an agent's own block is dropped, without that limit. Word both as dropped by submit, and say the mark is a convention, not a proof. The same holds for the red-first block; do not close the class for one key alone.
R3. commands/init.md step 4.5, the CHANGELOG entry and the README row say the user corrects a line in the same answer that approves the plan. The approval gate is a single-choice question, so a typed correction replaces the option and cannot also approve. Say that a correction is typed as the answer to the gate question, which presents the plan again.
R4. commands/init.md step 4.5 defines settled as said in the arguments or a step-2 answer; an answer given in step 3 or 3.5 then counts as unsettled. Define settled as said in the arguments or in any answer of steps 2 to 3.5.
R5. tests/test__refs.py case ia7 searches the whole of step 6 for the sentence that the approval gate prints the list; the sentence could move into a sub-step and the case stays green. Restrict the search to the text before the first sub-heading or code fence of step 6, and add a row that moves the sentence.
R6. tools/lints/_output_lints.py allows every file name under plugins/audit/evals as a name a test may carry, the git-ignored results directory included, so the orphan check can differ between a machine that ran an eval and one that did not. Skip that directory or read tracked files only, with one case.
R7, the part still open: the README row on the config hold says a linked worktree of the project and does not name a worktree nested under it, which the hook also covers.

FROM THE PHASE REVIEW, BY AREA.
Floor guard: a deleted fixture or support module under a test directory is reported as a deleted test; skip, assertion and suppression spellings of languages other than Python that the reader does not know; one file raising a recursion error, or one quoted path, turns the whole reading could-not-tell; a byte-order mark reads as does not compile; one unreadable accepted-suppression entry blanks every reading; an absent phase reads as clean (unconfirmed).
Green-first: scope with a tests-add entry re-derives expectRedFirst true on a green-first tdd task and the validator then refuses (unconfirmed); a re-opened task's base holds its own earlier commit (unconfirmed); the fallback block is worded for red and stamped with the green mark; a refusal of the green helper on the headless route is a bare repeating stop (unconfirmed); the landing does not re-read a green-first answer taken off an executor return.
Config hold: a relative path is resolved against the project, not the session directory, and the case named for it claims otherwise; a project root spelled through a symlink at another depth defeats the resolved-path comparison; for the main session the ask returns before the text rules, so a custom rule's block becomes a prompt; a task declaring the audit config dead-ends at the executor's first write with no notice when the task is added; a null floorGuard is clean to the validator and invalid to the schema.
Evals: the guard-stop refusal accepts a suite red for any reason; host git hooks run during the fixture build; the bugfix order grader fails a fix made with the Write tool or a relative path, and its before side is met by any call holding the word.
Clause reader: the last Acceptance item takes the prose after it, since only a heading ends it.

HOW TO PROVE. One case per finding, red on the tree before its fix; for a finding that does not reproduce, the command and its output in the outcome. A mutation probe covering every new case, runnable by the orchestrator. Documents changed here are read against the code they describe.

Acceptance:
(1) Each finding above is fixed with a case that was red before the fix, or is recorded in the outcome as not reproducing, with the run.
(2) No case that was green before this task is edited to pass; a case changed on purpose is named with the reason.
(3) The findings recorded on phase SG1 as R2 to R7 are each answered by name in the outcome.

ADDED BEFORE START 

FROM THE SECOND REVIEW ROUND (over the fix tasks; lows only - its med and high findings were fixed in SG1).
Floor guard: a declaration by path and test name also covers a method of that name in every class of the file (unless the ambiguity rule of the fix task already answers it - run it first).
Green-first: the signature of an executor return that is not JSON includes its absolute path, so a settlement made in another worktree is not honoured for it, against the docstring of the signature; the sentence the close of a phase prints about what is unsettled never asks about a waiting green-first answer; an existing case the task un-skips counts as a case of its own by the passed count.
Config hold: the drive's session mark set to 0 or to false counts as marked, so that session is refused where it should be asked.
Clause reader: an unfenced line starting with a hash inside a numbered list ends the body as a heading (the count is printed).
Eval grader: a git call behind a timeout prefix is not counted, and a comment holding a dry-run flag excuses a forced clean; the header of the case lists neither.

notes.text: More lows, left by the executors of the second round of SG1 fix tasks, to answer in this batch: (i) the header of plugins/audit/evals/guard-stop/case.yaml and two comments in tests/test_build_shop.py say the harness matches with JavaScript's regex engine and cite nothing - the plugin-evals documentation page says so in its grader table and its troubleshooting section (read 2026-11-18); name that page where the claim is made. (ii) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's sentence on tests/test_build_shop.py does not mention that the tripwire pattern is assembled from named parts in the suite or that it is timed. (iii) the greenFirst description in plugins/audit/schema/audit-plan.schema.json says nothing of a module that did not load or of the own-definitions count. Files this needs beyond the task's list: PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, plugins/audit/schema/audit-plan.schema.json.

Third-round lows (2026-11-18), each with a run probe under the session's review3 directory. (1) The eval tripwire counts a harmless git restore/clean/stash whose excusing option is quoted, escaped or continued on a second line; the bare forms were counted before SG1.28, the forms behind an escaped quote or a tab after 'then' are counted since - state it in the case file's header list of what may still count, or read the quoted option. (2) In the tripwire pattern a brace and a backtick are separators that the git path prefix and a NAME=value value also accept, so a long blank-free token of braces grows faster than linearly; under a third of a second at sixteen thousand characters. (3) Trailing prose after the last parenthesised Acceptance item joins that item without a word. (4) load_failures prints that the runner printed no reason for a bare stand-in line. (5) A staticmethod named test_ goes to the uncounted definitions. (6) jest and vitest: a todo test is counted as an own definition while the runner's todo figure is not among the skipped (read, not run).

Fourth-round lows on the floor guard and the config hold (2026-11-18), probes under the session's review4/x and review3/w directories. (1) One part of about ten thousand statements edited at both ends takes many seconds to pair (quadratic tables; synthetic). (2) tests/test_drive_phase.py is read by its definitions because one helper's name starts with the test prefix, so its labelled checks are never compared as units; an edited check there reads not compared, never a finding. (3) Renaming a function that holds checks, or adding a parameter to it, reports each check inside as moved; the word should say the enclosing statement changed. (4) The clean basis says no existing unit was compared after a row suite switches to the definitions reading. (5) A hard link placed in the project to the config of a tree outside it is not matched by the config hold; state it. (6) The walk up to find a directory that can answer the case question can cross a mount point. (7) A directory entry vanishing between the listing and the lookup reads as a volume that tells case apart. (8) On Windows a trailing dot or blank names the same file and is not matched by the config hold - read, not run; the owner's Windows machine can run it.

Fourth-round lows on green-first (2026-11-18), probes under the session's review4/y directory. (1) A definition repeated in one class is named twice in the basis. (2) The clause on kept files calls unchanged declared files anything the task changed. (3) A module-level helper whose name starts with the test prefix is taken out and listed as a case under unittest. (4) A file starting with a byte-order mark does not parse, so nothing is taken out of it. (5) A test assigned as a lambda is never taken out. (6) The schema's description of the greenFirst status does not say the baseline has the task's own definitions taken out, nor list the no-own-definition and flat-difference refusals. tasks.title: A tool call that failed still gets the pass after: the journal's sweep and the Bash-write notice run for a command that wrote and then exited non-zero
tasks.description:
READ FROM THE HOST'S DOCUMENTATION, NOT YET DRIVEN LIVE. The host's hooks reference (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, read 2026-11-18) says of the event this plugin registers its pass after under: it 'runs immediately after a tool completes successfully', and 'for tool calls that fail, add the same hook under PostToolUseFailure'; of that second event: it 'runs when a tool that started executing fails: the tool threw an error, or an MCP tool returned an error result', its sample payload is a test command with the error text 'Exit code 1', and 'cancelling a running tool does not fire this hook'. The plugin's hooks.json registers nothing under the second event. If the host behaves as documented, then for a command that writes and then exits non-zero - `sed -i ... file; false`, a script that edits the plan or the config and fails on a later line - no pass after runs: the journal's sweep writes no row for a config or plan file the command changed (the next call's pass before takes a fresh baseline, so the change is never a row; the trail check may warn later, and for a switch-off does not), and the Bash-write guard's after-the-fact notice - a block on the deny tier - is never given for an out-of-scope write. The orchestrator's probe of the journal with a pass before and no pass after shows no row and no warning. This predates this branch.

FIRST, ESTABLISH THE HOST'S BEHAVIOUR, and write down what was established and how: the documentation's sentences; the installed host's own binary or bundled schema naming the event and its payload fields; and what an older host does with an event name it does not know in a plugin's hooks.json - is the entry passed over, or is the plugin's whole hooks file refused. If the last cannot be established from documentation or the binary, stop and report: the registration then needs the owner's live run (hand over the exact command and the output that would settle it) and nothing is registered blind.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. EVERY HOOK REGISTERED FOR THE PASS AFTER IS ASKED ONCE WHETHER A FAILED CALL OWES ITS WORK, and the answer is written in one table beside the registration: the journal's sweep and the Bash-write notice owe it for a command and for an MCP tool; an edit tool that failed wrote nothing - say so from the host's documentation or leave it registered, whichever is established.
2. THE PASS AFTER DOES ITS WORK ONCE PER CALL whichever event carried it, and when a host sends both events for one call the second changes nothing: no second row, no second notice.
3. THE FAILED-CALL PAYLOAD IS READ AS WHAT IT IS: no tool response, an error text; nothing in the pass after may require the response's fields. A cancelled call fires nothing and is named in the documents as the case that leaves no row and no notice.
4. SECURITY.md's fail-mode table gains the rows the registration adds, by the rule the parity check holds it to; the README's hooks table, the build guide and the changelog follow; COMPATIBILITY.md says which host versions the registration needs, if the first step established one.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, each as the hooks run as processes with the failed-call payload: a command that edits the config and exits non-zero - no row; one that writes a file outside the running task's scope and exits non-zero - no notice; a switch-off by a failing command - no row. Allow twins: a failed command that wrote nothing leaves no row and no notice; both events for one call leave one row; a failed edit-tool call leaves none. The hook import budget holds. A mutation probe from the worktree root.

NOT in this task: a call that was cancelled; what the host does between events.

Acceptance:
(1) What the host does for a failed call, and what an older host does with the event's name, is written down with its source, or the task stopped and handed the owner the command.
(2) A command that changes a config or plan file and exits non-zero leaves its journal row, and one that writes outside the running task's scope and exits non-zero gets the notice.
(3) Both events for one call leave one row and one notice, and a failed call that wrote nothing leaves neither.
(4) SECURITY.md's fail-mode table matches hooks.json, and the documents name the cancelled call as the one that leaves nothing.

tasks.title: The integration branch holds the development branch as released and the phases landed on it since, with every conflict resolved to keep both sides' behaviour
tasks.description:
The skill-gates integration branch was cut from the development branch before the last release and before the phases that landed after it. Merging the development branch in conflicts in the files this task names: both sides appended changelog entries, build-guide sections, suite cases and plan records at the same places, and a few functions of the drive, the brief builder and the status facts were edited by both.

THE RULE. A merge commit of the development branch into the integration branch (no fast-forward), made by the orchestrator, not by an executor: git owns the merge state, and a scoped task commit cannot be made inside it. Each conflict is resolved to keep BOTH sides: appended entries and cases are kept from both, in the development branch's order first where order is free; a function edited by both carries both edits, and where the two cannot both stand the development branch's released behaviour wins and the skill-gates change is rebuilt on top of it. (1) The integration branch contains the development branch's head and no conflict marker remains in any tracked file.

tasks.title: The config hold's substituted-volume case and its disk-call count answer the same on every host, or say which host's half ran
tasks.description:
The first CI run over the skill-gates phase was red on two suites cases that are green on the machine they were written on (macOS, a volume that folds letter case). Both are cases of tests/test_guard_edits.py; the failing lines are quoted in the brief's notes.

MEASURED IN CI (ubuntu and windows runners), read from the job logs.
(a) cf31, named STUBBED, on ubuntu: the row 'dir-variant, top folds, .claude tells case apart' answered allow with NO question recorded, where it wants block and one identity question. On windows the same row answered block with no identity question, and the row 'dir-variant, top tells case apart, .claude folds' answered block where it wants allow. The case substitutes two questions of hooks/_config.py (_one_entry, _volume_folds) and its docstring says every host runs it; the path it drives (audit_config_way -> _names_audit_config -> _one_place) asks the REAL disk first - a stat of the written folder spelled in the other letter case, which exists on a folding volume and not on one that tells case apart, and a realpath that on windows returns the folder in its stored letter case. So the substituted model and the real volume disagree on two of three hosts. The orchestrator's reading, not yet proven by a run: the hold's real answers on each host are right and the case is what is host-bound.
(b) cf29 on windows: the row for a write that creates its file counted 5 disk calls now against 4 before identity was asked, so the case's 'no more in total than before' is false there; by kind it was realpath 2, stat 1 before the folder was resolved and islink 2, realpath 2, stat 1 now. On a posix host the realpath of the library is built from calls the counter counts and on windows it is not, so the two sides of the comparison are not the same measure on every host.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A case named STUBBED reaches no disk question it has not substituted, except one whose answer cannot differ between hosts (a path spelled as the config's own, in a directory the case made). Either drive the unit the model stands in for (the walk that judges one component in the directory holding it) or substitute every question on the driven path; a case that still depends on the host says so in its name and prints which host's half ran, and the other half is held by a real-volume case that runs where that volume exists.
2. What the hold answers END TO END for a folder or file name differing in letter case alone is asserted against the real volume the suite stands on, read from the disk and not from the platform's name: held where the volume folds, allowed where it tells case apart. Both halves must be reachable on at least one CI host each, and the suite's existing case-sensitive disk-image cases are the place to look before adding one.
3. A disk-call comparison compares two counts taken the same way on the host it runs on. Where a library call is built from counted calls on one host and not on another, the case counts what the hold itself asks (the calls its own source makes), or states the inequality per kind so the library's own cost is on neither side.
4. No behaviour of hooks/_config.py changes unless a run on a real volume shows the hold answering wrongly; if one does, stop and report it rather than changing the hold inside this task.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, reproduced locally: run the suite with its scratch space on a case-sensitive volume (a case-sensitive APFS disk image attached for the run and detached after, never a volume someone else attached) and show cf31 fail there as it does on ubuntu. Green after on both the folding system volume and the case-sensitive image. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root: the walk made to ask the wrong directory; the identity question dropped; the rule question answered for the wrong directory; a disk call added to the ordinary-write path. Windows cannot be run locally: state in the return exactly which lines depend on windows behaviour that only CI can confirm, and why they should hold.

NOT in this task: the hold's rule itself; the journal hook; any case not named here unless the same host dependence is shown in it by a run (then list it and fix it by the same rule).

Acceptance:
(1) The substituted-volume case gives the same verdicts and the same recorded questions on a folding volume and on one that tells case apart.

tasks.title: The eval builder's own-repository refusal is held on every host: what must never happen is asserted everywhere, and the check itself where git lets the patched builder reach it
tasks.description:
The first CI run over the skill-gates phase was red on windows in one case of tests/test_build_shop.py that is green on macOS and ubuntu.

MEASURED IN CI (windows runner), read from the job log. esc47 patches the shipped builder (plugins/audit/evals/build-shop.sh) to keep GIT_DIR, points GIT_DIR at another repository's .git, runs the bugfix scaffold and wants exit 3 with the words 'own repository' - the builder's check that the repository it built is the workspace's own. On windows the patched builder exited 2 with 'fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree | build-shop: git add failed': git itself refused before the builder's check was reached. Its neighbours esc45, esc46 and esc48 passed in the same job, so the shipped builder leaves the other repository alone there. Why git for windows refuses at that point (the form GIT_DIR arrives in under the shell that runs the builder, or how that git reads GIT_DIR with no work tree named) was NOT established - nothing here can run windows.

1. WHAT MUST NEVER HAPPEN IS ASSERTED ON EVERY HOST: a builder that kept GIT_DIR never exits 0, and the other repository is byte for byte and ref for ref what it was (the reading esc45 and esc46 already take).

Where git stops the patched builder first, the case does not pass silently and does not fail for git's reason: it prints that the check was not reached on this host, with git's words, as its own line a reader of a CI log can find.
3. THE CHECK IS ALSO HELD WITHOUT GIT'S HELP, on every host: one case drives the builder's own-repository check through an input that does not depend on how a git build reads GIT_DIR (for instance a patched builder whose build lands in the workspace while the question the check asks is answered for another repository), so the check has a red-first proof on windows too.

Say in the return which lines only a windows run can confirm.

(1) On every host a builder that kept GIT_DIR does not exit 0 and leaves the other repository unchanged.
(2) The own-repository check is asserted where reached, and a host where git stops first prints that as its own line.

tasks.title: The gate suite's byte-for-byte comparison of two runs masks a duration as one token, so how long a step took cannot turn it red
tasks.description:
The second CI run over the skill-gates phase (after the development branch was merged in) was red in tests/test_run_test_gate.py pgo7 on two legs - linux plain and windows cp1252 - and green in the same suite on linux stress, windows plain and macOS in the same run. The development branch's own CI was green on the commit that was merged. The case came in with that merge; nothing of the skill-gates line touches it.

WHAT THE CASE DOES (tests/test_run_test_gate.py, `_pgo_masked` and pgo7). It runs one task gate twice in two fixtures that differ only in a config value, masks 'ids, stamps and durations' out of what each printed, and wants the two texts equal. The mask's last step is `re.sub(r"\d+", "N", text)`.

THE ORCHESTRATOR'S READING, not yet proven by a red run - prove or refute it first. A step line prints its duration through `_fmt.human_duration` ("%d ms" below a second, "%.1f s" from one second, "%d m %02d s" from a minute) right-justified in a column. Masking the digits alone leaves two things that differ with nothing but time: the PADDING before a duration (a two-digit and a three-digit number of milliseconds, right-justified in one column, mask to texts with a different count of spaces in front) and the UNIT (`N ms` against `N.N s`). On this machine both runs take a two-digit number of milliseconds, so the case has only ever been seen green here; on a loaded runner the two runs land either side of a power of ten. The failing CI line prints only the exit codes, the entries run and the row keys - all equal for both runs - so the difference was in the masked text, which the line does not show.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. A duration is masked as ONE TOKEN WITH ITS PADDING, by what prints it: the mask recognises every form `_fmt.human_duration` can return (derive them from that function - call it over a range of values and build the expectation from its answers - rather than restating its three formats in the suite, so a fourth form added there is masked or turns a case red) and replaces the token and the column padding in front of it with one fixed word.
2. THE MASK IS HELD BY ITS OWN CASE, which needs no gate run: two texts that are one step line printed for durations either side of each boundary the formatter has (one and two digits, two and three, under and over a second, under and over a minute) mask to the same text; and two texts that differ in something that is NOT time (an entry name, an exit code, a word of a banner) do not - the allow half, so the mask cannot be widened into one that hides a real difference.
3. WHEN THE COMPARISON FAILS IT SHOWS THE DIFFERENCE: the failing line carries the differing lines of the two masked texts (a bounded unified diff), since a line that prints only what was equal sent a reader to the code.
4. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE. Search tests/ and tools/ for every other comparison of two runs' printed output that masks or ignores digits, stamps or durations by a pattern of its own (the starting grep: `re.sub(` beside `\\d` in tests/, and the words 'masked', 'byte for byte', 'the same lines'); list each in the return with whether a duration can reach it. One that can is moved to the same mask. If more than one suite needs it the mask lives in tests/_harness.py with its cases there - but another task of this phase is adding a helper to tests/_harness.py right before this one, so read the file as it stands when you start.
5. No behaviour of run-test-gate.py or _fmt.py changes.

HOW TO PROVE. Red before, locally: drive pgo7's comparison with a step whose duration is substituted (the fixture's command made to sleep, or the duration field substituted where the line is printed) so the two runs take 56 ms and 156 ms, then 950 ms and 1050 ms - the PRESENT mask reports them different. Green after with the same substitution. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root (a copy of the tree, each mutation asserted applied, __pycache__ purged between rows): the mask reverted to digits alone; the padding left out of the token; the mask widened to swallow the whole step line (the allow half goes red); the config value's effect made real - an always-firing split - so pgo7 still catches what it was written for.

NOT in this task: the growth-series timing cases (another task); the gate's own output.

Acceptance:
(1) Two runs whose steps took different numbers of digits of milliseconds, or fell either side of a second, compare equal under the mask; two that differ in anything else do not.
(2) The forms the mask knows are derived from the formatter, held by a case that needs no gate run.
(3) A failing comparison prints the differing lines.
(4) Every other masked comparison of two runs in tests/ and tools/ is listed, and one a duration can reach uses the same mask.

tasks.title: The eval builder refuses before its first git call when git is redirected to another repository, so a build that lost its unset writes nothing there on any host
tasks.description:
plugins/audit/evals/build-shop.sh builds an eval fixture as a repository of its own. Its header states the hazard: git exports GIT_DIR to a hook, so a build started from one would re-initialise and commit into the repository that name points at. Its defence is one line that unsets seven names before the first git call, and a check at the END of the build (`built()`) that refuses, exit 3, a build whose repository is not the workspace's own.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (2026-11-19 and -20; the orchestrator's prompt names the files). A copy of the builder with the unset line patched out, run with GIT_DIR naming another repository:
- macOS, git 2.53: the build adds and commits INTO THE OTHER REPOSITORY, and only then does the end check refuse with exit 3. The check detects; it does not prevent.
- windows runner, git 2.56.1.windows.1, GIT_DIR spelled as the host spells it (backslashes): the builder's `git init` REWRITES THE OTHER REPOSITORY'S CONFIG - `bare = false` becomes `bare = true` - and the next step fails with 'fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree', exit 2. The end check is never reached, and the other repository is left bare. With the same path spelled with forward slashes the init changes nothing and the add writes that repository's index and an object, as on macOS.
So on every host measured the second line of defence acts after the damage. The owner was asked and decided: the check moves ahead of the first write.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. BEFORE ITS FIRST GIT CALL THAT CAN WRITE - which is `git init`, not the first add - the builder asks whether the git it is about to run is redirected away from the workspace, and refuses with NOTHING WRITTEN ANYWHERE when it is. The question is asked independently of the unset line, so that line being lost, shortened or reordered is what the check catches.
2. WHICH NAMES REDIRECT GIT IS GIT'S ANSWER, NOT A LIST IN THE SCRIPT WHERE THAT CAN BE HAD: `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` prints the names git treats as repository-local. Decide, and say why in the header, between asking git for the names and keeping a written list - and note what that changes for the unset line itself, which today names seven and git's list is longer. ONE CONSTRAINT ON THAT: the suites run the builder with the sweep's own `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` pairs in the environment (they turn git's detached housekeeping off - CLAUDE.md, Tests), and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` and `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` are on git's list; a name that configures git without redirecting it to another repository must not be refused and must not be unset. State the rule that tells the two kinds apart rather than listing exceptions.
3. THE EXIT AND THE WORDS follow the header's own table, which stays true after the change: say which exit a refusal with nothing written is, and keep 'does not hold its own repository' for the end check, which stays as the last line of defence for what the early one cannot see (a repository that is not the workspace's for another reason - the suite's esc58 drives one).
4. tests/test_build_shop.py then asserts what the task before this one could not: for a builder that lost its unset, on every host, NOT exit 0 AND THE OTHER REPOSITORY BYTE FOR BYTE AND REF FOR REF WHAT IT WAS - unconditionally, with no 'unless the check refused' - and that the workspace was not written either. The cases added by the task before (esc47, esc57, esc58, esc59) are kept, tightened or folded as that requires; none is deleted without its assertion living on in another, and the return says where each went. The 'not reached on this host' line goes if no host can print it any more; say so.
5. THE PATH SPELLING IS A CASE, not a footnote: GIT_DIR spelled with backslashes and with forward slashes are both driven where the host has both spellings, and where it has one the case says which ran. The substituted git of esc59 stays as the way a refusing git is driven on a host that has none.
6. The shipped builder still builds both scenarios byte for byte as before when nothing redirects git: the committed ledgers and example fixtures derived from it do not change (`python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_build_shop.py`, and the scaffolds' own cases).

ALLOW CASES, as explicit as the refusal: a clean environment; a workspace nested inside another checkout (git would discover the parent - the build makes its own repository and that is right); the sweep's GIT_CONFIG_* pairs present; `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` or another name that is not repository-local.

HOW TO PROVE. Red first on the present builder: the new unconditional assertion fails on this host (the other repository's index and objects change). Green after. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root (a copy of the working tree, each mutation asserted applied, never `git archive HEAD`): the early check removed (the unconditional assertion goes red); the early check moved after `git init`; the early check asked through a wrapper that unset the names first (it can then never fire - the case that drives a lost unset goes red); the allow rows above each kept green under a check widened to refuse any GIT_ name. Say which lines only a windows run can confirm - the config rewrite cannot be reproduced here; describe how the case would catch it there.

NOT in this task: the timing cases of the same suite (esc53, esc55 - another task, next); the scaffolds' content.

Acceptance:
(1) A builder that lost its unset, run with git redirected to another repository, exits non-zero and leaves that repository and the workspace unwritten, on every host and for either path spelling, asserted unconditionally.
(2) The check sits before the first git call that can write and does not depend on the unset line.
(3) A clean environment, a nested workspace, the sweep's git config pairs and a non-repository GIT_ name all build as before.
(4) The header's exit table and its paragraph on the workspace's own repository say what the script now does.

tasks.title: The tripwire's growth is judged over a span of lengths wide enough that a host's change in per-character cost cannot read as backtracking, and a child that finished is never reported killed
tasks.description:
tests/test_build_shop.py esc53 was red on the windows runner in three CI runs out of three, before and after the timing helper of an earlier task (worst growth per doubling 5.38x, 5.68x, 5.98x against the 2 ** TRIPWIRE_POWER it allows), and green on linux and macOS every time. An earlier task read that as clock noise. It is not, and a scratch diagnostic on both runners measured why (the orchestrator's prompt names the two files; read them before anything else).

WHAT WAS MEASURED, machine idle, single searches on the fine wall clock and batches on processor time agreeing with each other:
- linux runner, python 3.12.16: every kind grows by about 1.8x to 2.4x per doubling from 200 to 3200 units. Linear.
- windows runner, python 3.12.10: the cost per character is LOWER than linux's at the short lengths and several times HIGHER at the long ones, with the change spread over roughly a decade of length. One kind read 63, 168, 670, 1984, 4398 microseconds at 200 to 3200 units - 2.7x, 4.0x, 3.0x, 2.2x per doubling; another 8.3x at one doubling in one process and 2.8x for the same doubling in the next. From 1600 to 3200 units the kinds whose text is longest are back near 2.2x. The whole span 200 to 3200 units (16 times the length) grew between about 59 and 89 times.
THE ORCHESTRATOR'S READING, to prove or refute by a run of your own on the diagnostic's numbers: this is a cost that is linear in two pieces with a steeper second piece (how that python build's allocator serves the engine's working memory once it passes a size), not backtracking - which would multiply by four at EVERY doubling without settling. A three-point series across the change cannot tell the two apart; that is the defect of the case, on that host.
- the same diagnostic: the python child alone takes between two and three seconds of wall on the windows runner for one kind, on an idle machine; in the red CI run the node child of the first kind was reported 'killed at the 10s deadline' although node alone answers in well under a second. `run_timers` starts both children together and gives each the time LEFT of one shared deadline, so a python child that used nearly all of it leaves node none, and on windows a `communicate` with no time left raises for a process that has already exited.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. GROWTH IS JUDGED OVER THE WHOLE SPAN, NOT PER DOUBLING: the time at the longest length over the time at the shortest is at most (the ratio of the two lengths) ** TRIPWIRE_POWER - the same power, unmoved - over a span wide enough that a bounded change in per-character cost cannot reach that bound and backtracking cannot miss it. Derive the span from the measurements and write the derivation where the constants are: the steepest change the diagnostic shows, the bound's room over it, and what a quadratic reads over the same span. The room must be stated as a ratio a reader can check against the diagnostic's numbers, and it must hold for every kind on both runners' numbers with at least a factor of two to spare; if no span gives that at lengths the engines can be asked, stop and say so with the numbers rather than choosing a thinner one.
2. The lengths are few (the cost of a series on a clock stepping 1/64 s is its number of lengths times its rounds), every engine is asked the same lengths, and the answers at every length are still judged (esc54, esc56). Check that node's engine answers at the longest length at all - a regular expression engine can refuse a long input in its own way - on the node this machine has, and say which node the runner has (the diagnostic prints it).
3. The absolute ceiling at the longest length and 'no child killed at its deadline' keep their meaning; if the longest length moves, the ceiling is re-derived from the diagnostic's per-character costs and the return carries the arithmetic. A deadline is raised only with the measured wall time that requires it beside it.
4. A CHILD THAT HAS EXITED IS NEVER 'KILLED'. Whatever time is left when its turn comes, a child that already finished is read, and only one still running at the deadline is killed and reported so. Each engine's deadline is its own or the shared one is honoured without starving the later child - choose, and hold the choice with a case that substitutes a slow first child and a fast second one and needs no real engine.
5. The cases still catch what they were written for: the tripwire made to backtrack turns the growth case red in both engines, on the real clock and on the substituted 1/64 s clock, and a kinked-linear cost - a substituted engine or a substituted series whose per-length times are the windows runner's own numbers - stays green. That last one is the allow case that was missing; it is driven from the diagnostic's numbers written into the case as history (measured where and when), not re-measured.
6. `_harness.growth_series` is not changed unless a run shows it must be; it is not among this task's files.

HOW TO PROVE. Feed the present judgement the windows runner's measured series: red (as CI). Feed the new one the same: green, with the room printed. The backtracking mutation: red under the new judgement. Suite seconds before and after, two runs with a gap, and the series' cost on the substituted 1/64 s clock (that is what windows will pay). A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root (a copy of the working tree, each mutation asserted applied, never `git archive HEAD`): the span narrowed back to the present three lengths; the power raised; the exited-child reading removed (the starved-child case goes red); the judgement made per doubling again (the windows-numbers allow case goes red). Say which lines only a windows run can confirm.

NOT in this task: the builder and its own-repository cases (the task before this one changes them - read the file as it stands); cw8 and gw15, which passed on the windows runner in the last CI run.

Acceptance:
(1) The growth judgement is over the whole span at TRIPWIRE_POWER, the span derived in writing from the two runners' measurements with at least a factor of two of room.
(2) The windows runner's measured series is green under it and a backtracking tripwire is red, in both engines.
(3) A child that has exited is read and never reported killed, held by a case that needs no real engine.
(4) No ceiling or deadline moved without the measurement that requires it.

tasks.title: A skill the plan pins reaches an agent or a session only as the bytes that were pinned: one reader of meta.skillPins, asked by every place that hands out a skill name
tasks.description:
WHAT IS TRUE TODAY (read from the tree, name the lines again before building on them). A plan names skills by string (meta.defaultSkills, meta.areas[*].skills, task.skills, and the review skill at three levels). The headless session runner (run-agent-session.py find_skills / load_skills) records the sha256 of each SKILL.md it loaded AFTER the fact and nobody compares it with anything; the subagent route hands the names to an agent in a brief (audit-lookup.py skills_lines, review_skill_lines) and reads no bytes at all. So a skill that was reviewed when it was vendored into .claude/skills can be changed, or shadowed by a personal copy of the same name (the resolver prefers personal over project, as Claude Code does), and every session after that follows the new text with nothing on the record.

THE RULE TO BUILD.
1. `meta.skillPins` (optional; a plan without the key behaves exactly as today, byte for byte in what it prints): an object keyed by skill name, each value `{"sha256": <digest>, "source": <free text, optional>}`. The schema, the manifest rules and validate-manifest.py know it; a pin for a name that is no skill name, or a digest that is not one, is a validation error.
2. THE DIGEST IS OF THE SKILL'S DIRECTORY, not of SKILL.md alone: SHA-256 over the sorted lines `<relative posix path> <sha256 of the file>` of every file under the directory that holds the SKILL.md the resolver found (the algorithm docs/research/benchmark-design.md section 4.2 already states for the benchmark's skill set). A checkout that converts line endings must answer the same digest as the one that pinned it: decide how (and say it where the digest is defined), prove it with a case, and say what that costs. A directory that cannot be read whole (a file unreadable, a link leading out of the directory, a directory too large to be a skill) has NO digest - that is a third answer, never a match.
3. ONE READER answers for one name: match / mismatch / not found in a place whose bytes can be read / could not be read, with the path it read and both digests. It lives beside `_skill_places.resolve_skill` and uses that resolver, so the copy judged is the copy a session would load. A pinned name the resolver cannot place (another plugin's skill, a skill bundled with Claude Code) cannot be verified, and a pin is a statement that the skill is a reviewed copy on disk - so that is a stop with its own words, not a pass.
4. EVERY PLACE THAT HANDS A SKILL NAME TO AN AGENT OR A SESSION ASKS THAT READER FIRST, for each pinned name it is about to hand out, and hands out nothing when one does not match: the headless runner does not start the session (it already refuses over a skill it cannot find - same exit, the reason names the skill, the path, the pinned and the found digest); the brief for a subagent is not composed and the drive stops before the dispatch line with the same reason, so no agent is spawned. An unpinned skill in the same task is untouched. Find the places by the code, not from this list: every caller of `_areas.resolve_skills` and `_areas.resolve_review_skill` that leads to a brief, a dispatch or a session either asks the reader or is named in the suite with the reason it need not (a status line that prints names hands nothing out). Hold that with a case that DERIVES the callers and fails for one that is neither - so a route added later cannot skip the pin silently.
5. A stop says what to do: restore the pinned bytes, or re-pin after reviewing the diff. It never offers to drop the pin as the way through.
6. WHAT THE PIN DOES NOT PROVE is written where the key is documented (README's config/manifest section, COMPATIBILITY.md, SECURITY.md): it proves the bytes are the ones pinned, not that they are safe; on the subagent route it verifies the copy the plugin's resolver finds and cannot see which copy Claude Code's Skill tool then loads; an unpinned skill is not checked at all. COMPATIBILITY.md: the key is new; list it under what is deliberately NOT yet promised (experimental until one vendored skill has been through a measured run), rather than widening the promise.

ALLOW CASES, as explicit as the stops: no skillPins key; a pin for a skill this task does not use; a pinned skill whose directory matches; the same skill resolved from the project when no personal copy exists; a checkout with converted line endings.

HOW TO PROVE. Red first for each stop (one changed byte in SKILL.md; one changed byte in a sibling file of the skill directory; a file added to the directory; a personal copy shadowing the pinned project copy; a pinned name found nowhere) on BOTH routes: the runner's exit and words, and the drive's `next` printing no dispatch line. A mutation probe the orchestrator can run from the worktree root (copy of the tree, each mutation asserted applied): the reader made to hash SKILL.md alone; the mismatch answer turned into a match; the runner's check removed; the brief's check removed; the caller-derivation case's exemption list widened to everything. Context ceilings (`python3 tools/measure-context.py --gate`) and the hook budget stay green; a new module, if any, gets its suite, layer and build-guide section (CLAUDE.md, Adding a .py).

NOT in this task: a verb that writes a pin and the doctor's row (the next task); how to vendor a skill (the task after); whether an unpinned missing skill is said on the subagent route (another task).

Acceptance:
(1) A plan without meta.skillPins prints and dispatches exactly as before.
(2) A pinned skill whose directory digest differs, or that is found nowhere its bytes can be read, starts no headless session and composes no subagent brief, and the reason names the skill, the path and both digests.
(3) The digest covers every file of the skill's directory and is the same on a checkout that converted line endings.
(4) Every caller that hands a skill name out asks the one reader, held by a case that derives the callers.
(5) The documents say what a pin does not prove, and COMPATIBILITY.md lists the key as not yet promised.
